question.text: Information rights in an AIF investment agreement typically include:

answer.text: Rights to receive regular financial statements, board meeting minutes, and other material information from the investee company
The right to publish investee company details publicly

explanation.text: The Logic: "Information rights" in an AIF investment agreement are contractual rights granted to the fund to receive regular and material information from the investee company — typically periodic (monthly/quarterly) financial statements, annual audited accounts, board meeting minutes, management reports, and notifications of material events. These rights allow the manager to monitor the investment over time. The Trap: Information rights are not access to classified government information, not access to competitor data, and do not permit public disclosure of investee company information — the AIF generally has confidentiality obligations. Note: The Series XIX-A AIF (Category I and II) Distributors workbook pages reviewed reference DDR virtual-data-room records and AIF reporting disclosures, but do not explicitly state that the investment agreement grants information rights to receive regular financial statements, board minutes and other material investee information. The framing above reflects general private-equity transaction practice rather than a workbook citation.
